admitted: The frozen 40-record population contains 92,160,000 signed-INT8 by binary-support signed-INT32 accumulators with zero mismatch against the exact float32 oracle.
The canonical 3090 run, an A800 cross-backend producer rerun, and an independently lowered A800 audit agree on every one of the 40 accumulator digests.
The two signed round-nearest-ties-even formulations agree on all 92,160,000 observed accumulators and naturally yield operator exception counts [0,0,0,1348].
The canonical LSB-first bitmap and arrivals-before-service FIFO thresholds are exact for the frozen abstract 96-lane vector stream.

findings.text: The population is ten samples and four bottleneck operators. Cross-sequence and full-network numerical coverage remains outside this milestone.
The FIFO values are exact only for one abstract 96-lane-vector-per-cycle stream with arrivals before service; tags, association latency, backpressure, and physical scheduling remain unimplemented.
This audit proves the binary-support/raw-convolution and late-scale integer bridge, not dynamic BatchNorm or end-to-end accuracy.

score_rationale: Full-population three-way agreement, explicit independent lowering, exact SHA closure, strict bitmap/FIFO recomputation, and two distinct GPU/software backends close the integer-oracle gate. Four points remain withheld because integration timing/RTL and broader numerical coverage are intentionally outside scope.
